package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised via a supply chain attack after an attacker gained access to a maintainer's npm account. Malicious versions were published that included code to reroute users' crypto transactions to an attacker-controlled wallet, resulting in direct financial theft from users interacting with dApps using the affected package.

execution_context.file_location: main bundle (UMD module) of the published package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code replaces the legitimate WalletConnect integration with a rogue version, intercepts user wallet connection attempts, and reroutes transaction signing to an attacker-controlled wallet, resulting in user funds being sent to the attacker's address.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and rerouting wallet connections to an attacker-controlled endpoint is a direct financial attack, as it subverts the intended transaction flow and results in theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal wallet connector packages should only facilitate secure connections between the user and their own wallet, never rerouting or intercepting private keys or transaction flows.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate wallet connector might swap out providers for testing or multi-wallet support, but never to a third-party, attacker-controlled endpoint in production.
key_indicators: Replacement of legitimate wallet connection logic with a rogue implementation
Network requests or transaction signing directed to unknown or attacker-controlled endpoints
No user consent or notification of wallet redirection

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to npm account of a former Ledger employee via phishing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish malicious package versions

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes malicious versions (1.1.5, 1.1.6, 1.1.7) of @ledgerhq/connect-kit to npm, embedding code that replaces the legitimate wallet connection logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to dApps and end users

attack_chain.action: When users interact with dApps using the compromised package, the malicious code executes at runtime, rerouting wallet connections and draining funds to the attacker's wallet.

behavioral_signatures: Runtime replacement of wallet connection logic
Network requests to unknown or non-standard wallet endpoints
Transaction signing or wallet connection without user consent
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in main bundle (UMD module) of @ledgerhq/connect-kit
References to non-official WalletConnect endpoints or modules
network_indicators: Transactions routed to non-user wallet addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected changes in wallet connection logic within packages, especially those that replace or proxy legitimate wallet providers. Flag any network requests or transaction flows directed to unknown endpoints or addresses not associated with the user. Use static analysis to detect code that imports or requires non-standard wallet modules, and runtime monitoring to catch unauthorized transaction redirection.
